findings.title: Recover saga state under both identity spellings
findings.why_it_matters: A crashed legacy saga can be missed when .2brain and .arsumbris coexist, leaving partially committed or dirty member trees unrecovered and allowing the identity migration to proceed despite an outstanding intent. When .2brain exists, saga_marker_dir selects it and the second array entry selects it again; startup recovery also checks only that selected directory. Read and recover both directories independently, including their preimages and failure sentinels.
findings.suggested_fix: Probe explicit .arsumbris/au-engine/run and .2brain/au-engine/run paths for intent and failure markers, and recover each existing journal without sweeping the other directory's preimages; test coexistence and both active journals.

findings.title: Do not silently skip supported claim syntax
findings.why_it_matters: Repositories with quoted YAML type claims or flow-list type claims can be reported as already migrated while still containing legacy engine identities. The splice treats a whitespace-delimited token such as 'au.engine.repo::au-engine' or [au.engine.repo::au-engine] as the entire name, so it does not match; the engine accepts list claims, and future removal of legacy aliases then breaks those files. Detect and rewrite every supported YAML claim form, or explicitly refuse unsupported forms instead of silently reporting success.
findings.suggested_fix: Use parsed YAML claim spans to splice quoted scalars and flow/block sequences, including all supported claim keys; explicitly report and refuse any unrepresentable claim before migration is marked complete.

findings.title: Restrict identity rewrites to actual claim fields
findings.why_it_matters: Running the migration can silently change user data that is not an engine identity claim. For example, an ordinary note's nested frontmatter mapping containing `example: { type: ... }` in block form is scanned just like its top-level type claim, and a legacy-looking nested value is rewritten and committed. Restricting splices to parser-identified claim nodes preserves unrelated YAML values.
findings.suggested_fix: Identify actual top-level instance type claims and type-definition claim fields from parsed YAML with source spans, and splice only those nodes; cover nested user values and YAML block scalar content.

findings.title: Report legacy claims in type definitions
findings.why_it_matters: An operator can see zero legacy-spelling hints while a type definition still contains an old `extends`, `sealed`, or required-meta claim, so the advertised release-window diagnostic cannot establish that removing compatibility is safe. Type-definition parsing canonicalizes those claims without collecting the legacy diagnostics that instance parsing emits. Emit the advisory on authored type-definition claims before canonicalization.
findings.suggested_fix: Collect legacy_spelling_diag for each type definition's parents, sealed and required_meta claims before canonicalizing, preserving the original source spans and adding release-window integration tests.

findings.title: Do not flag retained custom namespace identities
findings.why_it_matters: A legitimate user-defined `au.engine.custom` claim is reported as stale even when its canonical name is unchanged and `au migrate identity` cannot rewrite it. This makes the diagnostic gate noisy or permanently nonzero for a supported pre-migration tree and tells the operator to apply a fix that does nothing. Check whether canonicalization actually changes the authored claim before emitting the legacy warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit the diagnostic only when canonical_query_name differs from the authored claim, and test custom namespace claims with local and non-builtin repo qualifiers.

findings.title: Resolve rollback paths from the git worktree root
findings.why_it_matters: For a workspace member nested in a monorepo, rollback_preview can mark a dirty or superseded path clean and safe. `git diff-tree` returns worktree-root-relative names such as `tb-mcp-sdk/type/...`, but the checks run `git -C tb-mcp-sdk` with those names, making git check `tb-mcp-sdk/tb-mcp-sdk/type/...` instead. Run the history and cleanliness checks from the worktree root, and expose member-relative paths consistently.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the git worktree top-level once, perform all commit-tree, path-history and cleanliness queries relative to it, and translate output to the selected member's root; test dirty and subsequently changed paths in a nested member.

findings.title: Reject merge commits in rollback previews
findings.why_it_matters: A preview of a merge commit can return `safe: true` with no paths even though reverting the merge requires a mainline parent and would change files. The preview accepts multiple parents, takes the first, and invokes `git diff-tree` without a merge diff option, which produces no paths for a merge. Reject merges explicitly unless the API takes a mainline and computes that exact parent diff.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject commits with more than one parent as unsupported, or add an explicit mainline parent argument and derive the preview from that parent's tree; add a merge-commit integration case.

findings.title: Do not infer mutation history from current content
findings.why_it_matters: After a write succeeds and is subsequently reverted or overwritten, reconciliation reports `not_applied` and re-arms a retry even though the interrupted mutation did land. Conversely, matching bytes can predate the attempted operation. A current hash proves only current state, not historical outcome; a caller relying on the advertised result may undo a deliberate rollback or repeat an already-applied action.
findings.suggested_fix: Track a durable mutation ID and its commit/compensation state to answer historical application, or return an explicit unknown/diverged outcome whenever history cannot prove the result; describe the current hash separately and do not imply a retry is safe.

findings.title: Avoid shadowing legacy state during fallback installation
findings.why_it_matters: A pre-migration installation can lose access to its existing registry and daemon socket immediately after the installer falls back to its private engine path. Creating `$HOME/.2brain/bin` makes `.2brain` exist, so the engine's state-root resolver prefers the newly empty directory over the populated `$HOME/.arsumbris`, rather than continuing to read the legacy state. This occurs when 2brain installs but replacing `au` fails, such as an executing au binary on Linux.
findings.suggested_fix: Install the fallback binary outside the state-root namespace, or resolve the existing state root with the same 2BRAIN_HOME/new/legacy precedence before creating directories; test an existing legacy-only home with a refused au replacement.

findings.title: Fail all-repository migration on unreadable registries
findings.why_it_matters: A migration requested with `--all` can silently omit every repository in an unreadable or malformed registry and still succeed, or fall back to scanning the current directory as though it were the requested set. The shared registry parser deliberately degrades bad YAML to an empty map, and this caller also discards file-read errors. A success report therefore cannot establish that all registered repositories were migrated.
findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish absent optional registry files from unreadable or malformed ones, fail --all on invalid present inputs, and never substitute the current directory merely because the requested registry set is empty.
